title: Developer Cost Pulse — PRD & Launch Plan
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This PRD describes Developer Cost Pulse: a lightweight, developer-facing real-time cost monitoring and alerting surface that lives in the Redwood Console and SDKs. Cost Pulse surfaces anomalies, per-route cost regressions, session-level hotpaths, and suggested mitigation actions targeted at developer workflows (local sandbox, staging, and early production). The product is intended to reduce surprise invoices, accelerate developer troubleshooting, and make cost impacts actionable without requiring deep infra or finance involvement.

Goals

- Give developers immediate, contextual visibility into surprising token and embedding costs at the route/session level.
- Provide deterministic, low-friction remediation steps and SDK/console links (e.g., sample prompt changes, model downgrade suggestions, quantization toggles).
- Enable a 30–60 day pilot with selected customers to validate alert precision, false-positive rate <= 15%, and 20% reduction in unexpected spend incidents during pilot.

Non-goals

- Replace infra-level billing reconciliation or month-end invoicing.
- Full-chargeback accounting for all enterprise customers on day one.

User personas

- Developer (Primary): integrates Redwood API, needs quick feedback on cost regressions and guidance.
- Platform/Infra engineer: wants signals for systemic inefficiencies across routes.
- Finance/Customer Success: consumes rollup reports and pilot summaries.

User stories

1) As a developer, I receive a Console notification when a route's per-call median token cost increases by >30% for 24 hours.
2) As a developer, I can open a session-level view showing the exact prompts and model variant that produced the anomaly, with suggested mitigations (shorten prompt, switch to faster model variant, enable lightweight quantization).
3) As a platform engineer, I can subscribe to aggregated alerts across a workspace to detect global regressions.

Functional requirements (MUST)

1. Real-time detection pipeline: ingest per-request telemetry (model, route, tenant, seq_len, tokens_in/out, embeddings_units, latency, kernel_tag) and compute rolling baselines (7-day & 30-day).
2. Alerting rules engine: support both statistical (z-score / median absolute deviation) and rule-based (absolute threshold) triggers.
3. Developer Console surface: a compact "Pulse" panel per-route showing trend sparkline, current per-call unit cost, trigger reason, and one-click remediation suggestions.
4. SDK integration: lightweight client library method (costPulse.reportSample) to tag debug annotations and opt-in sampling for dev-mode.
5. Sampling and retention: default 100% sampling in sandbox/staging; 1% sampling in production (configurable per-tenant).
6. Permission model: Console view respects role-based permissions; cost alerts can be scoped to team owners.

Functional requirements (SHOULD/COULD)

- Suggested mitigations include: recommended max_prompt_length, suggested model variant (cost/latency tradeoff), and quantization profile link.
- Auto-created support ticket template for escalations including a reproducible minimal promptset.
- Integration with Optimize suggestions to simulate the cost impact of proposed mitigations.

Success metrics (KPIs)

- Pilot reduction in “unexpected spend” incidents: >=20% reduction for pilot clients within 60 days.
- Alert precision: true positive rate >= 85% during pilot.
- Developer action rate: >= 25% of actionable alerts lead to an in-console mitigation or a runbook link click within 72 hours.
- Time-to-detect: median detection latency <= 10 minutes for anomalies above threshold.

Telemetry and observability

- Required fields ingested per-request: timestamp, workspace_id, route_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, embeddings_units, response_status, seq_len, kv_cache_hit, latency_ms.
- Metrics exposed to SRE: pulse.alerts.count, pulse.alerts.true_positives, pulse.alerts.false_positives, pulse.detection.latency_ms, pulse.sampling.rate_per_tenant.

Architecture & integrations

- Detection pipeline will be a stream job (existing telemetry ingestion -> new pulse processor). Preferred stack: kinesis -> Flink/Beam job -> anomaly store.
- Console UI: new small React widget in the route details page. Widget calls a Pulse service endpoint (read-only) with cached results (TTL 60s).
- SDK: JS/TS and Python bindings add opt-in sample reporting; SDK calls are off-path and buffered to avoid request tail latency.
- Data retention policy: sampled raw evidence retained 30 days; aggregated baselines retained 365 days.

Privacy and compliance

- All sampled prompts must be masked by default; full prompt storage requires explicit tenant consent (billing/diagnostics opt-in).
- Compliance owners must review retention and masking defaults for regulated customers.

Rollout plan & timeline (high level)

1. Q1 (4 weeks): Implementation spike — detection algorithm prototypes and sampling integration; define API contract for pulse.read and pulse.metadata.
2. Q2 (6 weeks): Core pipeline and alerting rules engine; Console widget mock -> usability review.
3. Q3 (4 weeks): Pilot with 3 selected customers and 5 internal Redwood product teams; collect feedback and false-positive telemetry.
4. Q4 (3 weeks): Iteration, Optimize integration, and GA readiness (documentation, runbooks, pricing guidance).

Pilot criteria and gating

- Pilot goes to GA if: pilot customers report <15% false-positive alerts, and measurable reduction in unexpected-spend incidents >=20%.
- Security review and data retention approvals must be completed before pilot when customer-supplied prompts are opted into sampling.

Operational playbooks (developer facing)

1. When an alert fires, developer opens Pulse detail -> quick diagnostics: "Top 3 contributing prompts" and "Suggested action".
2. If the action is to change to a cheaper variant, Console shows estimated monthly cost delta and a link to change route config.
3. If the developer tags the alert as "not useful", the event is recorded to tune detection parameters (feedback loop).

Pricing & packaging notes (initial position)

- Pulse is included in all paid tiers during pilot. For GA consider a freemium model where basic live alerts are included and advanced features (per-call evidence retention, Optimize-sim integration, and automatic remediation tickets) are part of an "Optimize Insights" add-on.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, Pulse can run as a packaged telemetry connector; additional storage or retention SLAs are add-ons.

Open questions & risks

- Detection accuracy on low-volume routes: how do we avoid both noisy signals and missed regressions? Proposed mitigation: hybrid rules with min-sample thresholds.
- Prompt privacy: customer acceptance of prompt sampling in diagnostics. Mitigation: default masking + explicit opt-in UX and audit logs.
- Cost: storage and processing of sampled evidence for large customers; mitigation: tiered sampling and retention, pilot-specific quotas.

Ownership & next steps

- Product owner: Asha Patel (product)
- Engineering leads: Daniel Kim (platform), Marta Rodriguez (console)
- SRE/Telemetry contact: Ethan Li

Next steps (this doc)

1. Approve detection algorithm proposal (2 weeks).
2. Kickoff engineering spike and finalize pipeline contract (4 weeks).
3. Recruit pilot customers and prepare pilot contract language with CS (6 weeks).
